Ramsar Convention

📍 Ramsar, Iran
🎯 Target: Wetlands
🇮🇳 India: Joined 1981

Conservation & wise use of wetlands.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe first major global treaty devoted specifically to wetlands. It promotes conservation and the ‘wise use’ of wetlands rather than simply banning their use.
Key provisions / mechanismWetlands are identified as internationally important sites using agreed criteria. Parties are expected to maintain the ecological character of listed sites and promote wise use of wetlands throughout their territory.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia became a Contracting Party in 1981. India designates Ramsar Sites and participates in international wetland conservation.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionRamsar is a convention on wetlands; it is not a treaty specifically about migratory birds. The Ramsar Convention was adopted in Ramsar, Iran.
LINK IT: Wetlands • Ramsar Sites • wise use • ecological character
KEY: WETLANDS • Year: 1971

Stockholm Conference

📍 Stockholm, Sweden
🎯 Target: Human environment
🇮🇳 India: Participated

First major UN conference on the human environment; led to UNEP.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe 1972 United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was a landmark in international environmental governance.
Key provisions / mechanismIt produced the Stockholm Declaration and an Action Plan and helped lead to the creation of UNEP. 5 June is observed as World Environment Day, linked to the opening of the conference.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia participated; Prime Minister Indira Gandhi spoke at the conference and highlighted the relationship between poverty and environmental concerns.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionDo not confuse the 1972 Stockholm Conference with the 2001 Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants.
LINK IT: 1972 • Human environment • UNEP • World Environment Day
KEY: ENVIRONMENT • Year: 1972

World Heritage Convention

📍 Paris, France
🎯 Target: Cultural & natural heritage
🇮🇳 India: Joined 1977

Protects cultural and natural heritage of outstanding universal value.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersUNESCO convention for identifying and protecting cultural and natural heritage considered to have outstanding universal value.
Key provisions / mechanismStates identify and nominate sites; the World Heritage Committee considers inscription on the World Heritage List. It covers cultural, natural and mixed heritage.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia accepted the convention in 1977 and has numerous World Heritage properties.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionWorld Heritage Convention is about heritage protection, not biodiversity alone. UNESCO is the specialised UN agency associated with it.
LINK IT: UNESCO • World Heritage List • cultural heritage • natural heritage

CITES

📍 Washington, D.C., USA
🎯 Target: International wildlife trade
🇮🇳 India: Joined 1976

Regulates international trade in wild animals and plants so trade does not threaten species.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersCITES prevents international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants from threatening their survival.
Key provisions / mechanismSpecies are placed in Appendices with different levels of trade regulation. International commercial trade in Appendix I species is generally prohibited except under limited circumstances; Appendix II permits regulated trade with required documentation.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia became a party in 1976 and implements CITES-related controls through its wildlife and customs framework.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionCITES regulates international trade; it does not itself ban every use or domestic trade of every endangered species.
LINK IT: Appendix I • Appendix II • Appendix III • permits • wildlife trade
KEY: WILDLIFE TRADE • Year: 1973

CMS / Bonn Convention

📍 Bonn, Germany
🎯 Target: Migratory species
🇮🇳 India: Joined 1983

Conservation of migratory animals and their habitats through international cooperation.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals focuses on animals that cross national boundaries during migration.
Key provisions / mechanismIt promotes international agreements and coordinated conservation for migratory species and their habitats. Species are listed in different appendices according to conservation concern.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia became a party in 1983 and participates in conservation initiatives for migratory species and their habitats.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionCMS/Bonn = migratory species. CITES = international wildlife trade. Ramsar = wetlands.
LINK IT: Migratory species • habitats • international cooperation

Vienna Convention

📍 Vienna, Austria
🎯 Target: Ozone layer protection
🇮🇳 India: Party

Framework for international cooperation to protect the ozone layer.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersCreates the international framework for cooperation on scientific research, observation, information exchange and measures to protect the ozone layer.
Key provisions / mechanismIt established the institutional and scientific framework that supported later control measures. It does not contain the detailed substance phase-out schedules associated with the Montreal Protocol.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a party to the Vienna Convention and participates in the global ozone-protection regime.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionVienna = framework; Montreal = phase-out of ozone-depleting substances. Kigali = HFC phase-down.
LINK IT: Ozone layer • Vienna 1985 • Montreal 1987 • Kigali 2016
KEY: OZONE • Year: 1985

Montreal Protocol

📍 Montreal, Canada
🎯 Target: Ozone-depleting substances
🇮🇳 India: Party

Phases out controlled ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs; Kigali later added HFC phase-down.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersA landmark treaty designed to phase out production and consumption of controlled ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
Key provisions / mechanismIt uses control schedules, reporting, trade controls and financial/technical assistance mechanisms. Major ODS include CFCs and halons. It has been adjusted and amended several times.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a party and has implemented ODS phase-out measures. India’s compliance is important because developing-country schedules can differ from developed-country schedules.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionMontreal targets ODS. HFCs generally do not deplete ozone but were brought under a phase-down through the Kigali Amendment because of their high global-warming potential.
LINK IT: CFCs • ODS • ozone hole • Kigali Amendment • Multilateral Fund
KEY: OZONE • Year: 1987

Basel Convention

📍 Basel, Switzerland
🎯 Target: Hazardous waste
🇮🇳 India: Joined 1992

Controls transboundary movement and disposal of hazardous wastes.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersControls the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal, with the goal of protecting human health and the environment.
Key provisions / mechanismIt uses notification and consent procedures for covered transboundary movements and promotes environmentally sound management. The Basel Ban Amendment strengthens restrictions on certain hazardous-waste exports from developed to developing countries.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia became a party in 1992 and regulates hazardous-waste movement through domestic rules and international obligations.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionBasel is not simply ‘the plastic convention’. It is principally associated with hazardous waste and transboundary movement; plastic-waste controls were later strengthened within the Basel framework.
LINK IT: Hazardous waste • transboundary movement • prior notification • environmentally sound management
KEY: HAZARDOUS WASTE • Year: 1989

Rio Earth Summit

📍 Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
🎯 Target: Sustainable development
🇮🇳 India: Participated

Major 1992 Earth Summit; associated with Agenda 21, UNFCCC and CBD.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) placed sustainable development at the centre of global environmental policy.
Key provisions / mechanismMajor outcomes included Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, the UNFCCC and the Convention on Biological Diversity; it also strengthened global attention to sustainable development and forests.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia participated and continues to emphasise development needs, equity and differentiated responsibilities in international environmental negotiations.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionRio 1992 is an event/conference, while UNFCCC and CBD are conventions adopted/opened for signature at the same broad process.
LINK IT: Agenda 21 • Rio Declaration • UNFCCC • CBD • sustainable development
KEY: RIO SUMMIT • Year: 1992

UNFCCC

📍 Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
🎯 Target: Climate change
🇮🇳 India: Party

Framework to address climate change and stabilize greenhouse-gas concentrations.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe core international framework for addressing climate change by stabilising greenhouse-gas concentrations at a level that avoids dangerous human interference with the climate system.
Key provisions / mechanismIt established principles including equity and CBDR-RC and created the COP process. The Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement developed under this climate regime.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and consistently highlights equity, climate justice and CBDR-RC. India communicates its climate targets through NDCs.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionUNFCCC is the framework convention; Kyoto is a protocol with quantified targets for certain developed countries; Paris uses nationally determined contributions for all Parties.
LINK IT: Climate • GHGs • COP • CBDR-RC • NDCs
KEY: CLIMATE • Year: 1992

Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)

📍 Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
🎯 Target: Biodiversity
🇮🇳 India: Party

Conservation, sustainable use and fair & equitable benefit sharing from genetic resources.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersA comprehensive treaty built around conservation of biodiversity, sustainable use, and fair and equitable benefit sharing from genetic resources.
Key provisions / mechanismIts three objectives are conservation, sustainable use, and fair/equitable benefit sharing. The Cartagena Protocol addresses biosafety; the Nagoya Protocol addresses access and benefit sharing.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and enacted the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 to implement domestic biodiversity governance, including access and benefit-sharing mechanisms.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionCBD = biodiversity. Cartagena = biosafety/LMOs. Nagoya = access and benefit sharing.
LINK IT: Conservation • sustainable use • genetic resources • Cartagena • Nagoya
KEY: BIODIVERSITY • Year: 1992

DESERTIFICATION
🏜️💧
DRYLAND + DROUGHTUNCCD → Desertification

UNCCD

📍 Paris, France
🎯 Target: Desertification / land degradation
🇮🇳 India: Party

Combats desertification, land degradation and drought.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersAddresses desertification, land degradation and drought, especially in drylands, through sustainable land management and international cooperation.
Key provisions / mechanismIt promotes integrated strategies, sustainable land management, drought resilience and participation of affected communities. Land degradation neutrality is an important contemporary policy concept.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and hosted UNCCD COP14 in New Delhi in 2019.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionDesertification does not mean expansion of deserts only; it refers to land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas caused by climatic and human factors.
LINK IT: Desertification • drought • land degradation • drylands • LDN
KEY: DESERTIFICATION • Year: 1994

Kyoto Protocol

📍 Kyoto, Japan
🎯 Target: GHG emission reduction
🇮🇳 India: Non-Annex I; no binding target under original targets

Legally binding targets applied mainly to developed/Annex I parties in its first commitment period; CDM is a key mechanism.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersAdopted under the UNFCCC, Kyoto established legally binding greenhouse-gas reduction targets for many developed/Annex I Parties during its commitment periods.
Key provisions / mechanismImportant mechanisms included International Emissions Trading, Joint Implementation and the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM). The principle reflected differentiated responsibilities.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia was a Non-Annex I developing country and did not have a binding quantified emission-reduction target under the original Kyoto targets. India hosted and participated in CDM projects.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionDo not say Kyoto imposed the same binding reduction target on all countries. Paris later moved to NDCs for all Parties.
LINK IT: Annex I • Non-Annex I • CDM • carbon market • GHG
KEY: CLIMATE • Year: 1997

Convention on Supplementary Compensation (CSC)

📍 Vienna / Brussels framework
🎯 Target: Nuclear damage compensation
🇮🇳 India: India joined 2016

Provides a framework for supplementary compensation following nuclear damage.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersProvides a framework for supplementary compensation for nuclear damage, helping ensure availability of funds beyond the operator’s primary liability under applicable national law.
Key provisions / mechanismIt supplements national compensation arrangements and aims to establish a minimum national compensation amount and additional international funds from contracting parties.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia joined the CSC in 2016, strengthening its position in the international nuclear liability framework.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionCSC is about civil liability and compensation for nuclear damage, not nuclear non-proliferation or radioactive-waste disposal.
LINK IT: Nuclear damage • civil liability • compensation • supplementary funds
KEY: NUCLEAR DAMAGE • Year: 1997

Rotterdam Convention

📍 Rotterdam, Netherlands
🎯 Target: Chemicals & pesticides
🇮🇳 India: Party

Promotes shared responsibility through the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersPromotes shared responsibility in international trade of certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides through the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure.
Key provisions / mechanismExporting countries must ensure information and notifications; importing countries can make informed decisions about future imports of listed chemicals. The PIC procedure improves information flow and national decision-making.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and participates in the PIC system for covered chemicals and pesticides.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionRotterdam = PIC/chemicals/pesticides. Basel = hazardous waste. Stockholm = POPs.
LINK IT: PIC • hazardous chemicals • pesticides • informed decision
KEY: CHEMICALS • PIC • Year: 1998

Cartagena Protocol

📍 Montreal, Canada
🎯 Target: Biosafety / LMOs
🇮🇳 India: Party

Biosafety framework for living modified organisms, including safe handling, transport and use.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersA biosafety protocol under the CBD dealing with living modified organisms (LMOs) that may have adverse effects on biodiversity, also taking account of risks to human health.
Key provisions / mechanismIt establishes procedures for transboundary movement, including the Advance Informed Agreement (AIA) procedure for certain LMOs intended for intentional introduction into the environment.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and regulates biosafety and genetically engineered organisms through its domestic regulatory framework.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionCartagena = biosafety/LMOs. Nagoya = access and benefit sharing. CITES = wildlife trade.
LINK IT: LMOs • biosafety • AIA • modern biotechnology • CBD
KEY: BIOSAFETY • Year: 2000

Stockholm Convention

📍 Stockholm, Sweden
🎯 Target: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)
🇮🇳 India: Ratified 2006

Targets persistent organic pollutants that persist, bioaccumulate and travel long distances.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersTargets Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), chemicals that persist in the environment, can bioaccumulate and biomagnify, and can travel long distances.
Key provisions / mechanismParties work to eliminate, restrict or reduce production and releases of listed POPs. The treaty includes measures for unintentionally produced POPs and waste/stockpiles.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia ratified the convention in 2006 and participates in global POPs management.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionStockholm Convention (2001) ≠ Stockholm Conference (1972). This is one of the most important SSC confusion pairs.
LINK IT: POPs • persistence • bioaccumulation • biomagnification

ITPGRFA

📍 Rome, Italy
🎯 Target: Plant genetic resources
🇮🇳 India: Party

Conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture, with benefit sharing.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersThe International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture supports conservation and sustainable use of crop genetic diversity.
Key provisions / mechanismIt creates a Multilateral System for facilitated access to specified plant genetic resources and a benefit-sharing framework for food and agriculture.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and has strong relevance because of its crop diversity and plant genetic resources.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionITPGRFA is specifically about plant genetic resources for food and agriculture, not all genetic resources.

Nagoya Protocol

📍 Nagoya, Japan
🎯 Target: Access & Benefit Sharing
🇮🇳 India: Party

Fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from use of genetic resources.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersImplements the CBD objective of fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources.
Key provisions / mechanismIt establishes rules around access, mutually agreed terms and compliance, including recognition of access permits and domestic requirements.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia is a Party and uses its biodiversity legislation and institutional mechanisms for access and benefit sharing.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionNagoya = ABS. Cartagena = biosafety. Remember both are protocols to the CBD.

Minamata Convention

📍 Kumamoto, Japan
🎯 Target: Mercury pollution
🇮🇳 India: Signed 2014; ratified 2018

Controls anthropogenic mercury supply, trade, use, emissions and releases to protect health and environment.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersProtects human health and the environment from anthropogenic emissions and releases of mercury and mercury compounds.
Key provisions / mechanismCovers mercury supply and trade, products and processes using mercury, emissions to air, releases to land/water, storage, waste and contaminated sites.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia signed in 2014 and ratified in 2018; domestic measures address mercury-containing products and emissions.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionMinamata is named after the Japanese city associated with severe mercury poisoning. Keyword = Mercury.
LINK IT: Mercury • Minamata disease • emissions • releases • health

Paris Agreement

📍 Paris, France
🎯 Target: Climate change
🇮🇳 India: Party / NDCs

Keep warming well below 2°C and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C; all parties submit nationally determined contributions.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersA legally binding climate treaty under the UNFCCC that strengthens the global response to climate change and aims to hold warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts toward 1.5°C.
Key provisions / mechanismAll Parties prepare and communicate NDCs, update them over time, report progress and participate in a global stocktake. It also covers adaptation, finance, technology and capacity-building.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia submitted NDCs and has announced a long-term net-zero target for 2070. India stresses equity, climate justice and CBDR-RC.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionParis does not assign one identical emission-cut percentage to every country. Targets are nationally determined.
LINK IT: NDCs • 1.5°C • 2°C • global stocktake • net zero
KEY: CLIMATE • Year: 2015

Kigali Amendment

📍 Kigali, Rwanda
🎯 Target: HFC phase-down
🇮🇳 India: Ratified 2021

Phases down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) under the Montreal Protocol because of their high global-warming potential.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersAmends the Montreal Protocol to phase down HFCs, which are powerful greenhouse gases used in refrigeration and air-conditioning.
Key provisions / mechanismCountries follow differentiated HFC phase-down schedules. It is a phase-down, not an ozone-depletion phase-out, because HFCs generally have little or no ozone-depleting effect.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021 and follows the schedule applicable to developing-country groups.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionMontreal = ODS/ozone. Kigali = HFCs/climate. HFCs replaced many ODS but have high global-warming potential.
LINK IT: HFCs • refrigeration • cooling • global warming potential
KEY: HFCs • Year: 2016

Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework

📍 Kunming / Montreal
🎯 Target: Global biodiversity targets
🇮🇳 India: Supports framework

Global biodiversity framework under the CBD; includes the 30×30 conservation ambition for 2030.

📖 Detailed SSC Notes
Why it mattersA global biodiversity framework adopted under the CBD to guide action to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030 and toward 2050.
Key provisions / mechanismIt contains 4 global goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030. The famous ‘30×30’ ambition seeks effective conservation and management of at least 30% of terrestrial/inland water and marine/coastal areas by 2030.
🇮🇳 India focusIndia supports the framework and works through its national biodiversity policies and targets.
⚠️ SSC trap / distinctionIt is a framework under the CBD, not a completely separate convention. It was adopted at CBD COP15 in 2022.
LINK IT: 30×30 • biodiversity loss • 2030 targets • CBD COP15
KEY: 30×30 • Year: 2022
